title: Nothing that looks like a placeholder
statement: Never ship anything that looks like a placeholder: use the real asset, or redesign the page without it and note what is missing.
detail: The rule followed an emoji in a circle standing in for a character's art in a one-lesson build. It asks for the real program asset first; if that can't be obtained, the element is removed or the layout redesigned so the page looks complete without it, and the omission is recorded in the build notes, with no emoji stand-ins, empty art boxes or filler text. The reason given is that a placeholder reads as not ready and spoils otherwise strong work.

evidence.quote: never ship placeholder-looking elements; if an asset can't be obtained, admit it in notes and redesign the layout honestly instead
